werk/epica-design-your-universe.text:
Design Your Universe is Epica's fourth studio album, released on 16 October 2009. It was the first record with guitarist Isaac Delahaye and drummer Ariën van Weesenbeek as official members. Recording began on 2 March 2009 at Gate Studio in Wolfsburg, with the familiar collaborators Sascha Paeth, Amanda Somerville and Miro Rodenberg. Where its predecessor was about religions, this record revolves around the power of thought and imagination, inspired by new insights from quantum physics, said Mark Jansen.

Three tracks continue the series A New Age Dawns. On White Waters, Tony Kakko of Sonata Arctica sings a duet with Simone Simons; his part was recorded in Finland. Incentive is one of the few tracks without Simons. The reception was positive, and the record reached number eight on the Dutch chart, the highest for the band up to then.
werk/epica-design-your-universe.listen: Listen to White Waters and notice how the voices of Simone Simons and Tony Kakko come together in the duet.

werk/epica-the-divine-conspiracy.text:
The Divine Conspiracy is Epica's third studio album and their first concept album. It was released in 2007 on Nuclear Blast. The idea is that God created many religions so that people would discover that at heart they are the same. At the same time the record completes the series The Embrace That Smothers, about the dangers of organised religion. After drummer Jeroen Simons left in 2006, Ariën van Weesenbeek played as a guest.

Many themes come from the news. Safeguard to Paradise is about convincing suicide bombers, in sharp contrast with the gentle music. Beyond Belief is about the conflict between science and religion, without taking sides. Death of a Dream tells of a young Muslim woman who was killed by her father, with grunts by Sander Gommans. It was the band's first album in the Dutch top ten, at number nine.
werk/epica-the-divine-conspiracy.listen: Listen to Death of a Dream and notice the contrast between Simone Simons's singing and Sander Gommans's grunts.

werk/erasure-the-innocents.text:
The Innocents is the third album by the English synth-pop duo Erasure, Vince Clarke and Andy Bell. It was released in April 1988 and produced by Stephen Hague. The record was the group's breakthrough: in the United Kingdom it became the first number 1 album in a long series for them, and in the United States heavy exposure on MTV produced two big hits on the Billboard Hot 100.

The album opens with four strong tracks in a row: A Little Respect, Ship of Fools, Phantom Bride and Chains of Love. They combine big melodies with the synthesizers for which the duo became known. According to the source, the album also became a beloved part of queer club music. The cover shows a stained-glass window from Chartres Cathedral. To date this is the duo's best-selling album, with an estimated five million copies worldwide.
werk/erasure-the-innocents.listen: Listen to A Little Respect and notice the role of the synthesizers: how do the repeating rhythms and the vocals make the chorus so catchy?

werk/erasure-wonderland.text:
Wonderland is the debut album of the English synth-pop duo Erasure and was released on 1 May 1986 on Sire Records in the United States and on 2 June on Mute Records in the United Kingdom and Germany. Vince Clarke, who had earlier had success with Depeche Mode and Yazoo, formed the duo with singer Andy Bell, who names Alison Moyet as an influence on his voice.

The album was not an immediate success. The three singles failed to reach the top forty in the United Kingdom, although the record did better in Germany and Sweden. In the United States two singles reached the top ten of the dance club chart. Billboard called Reunion and Oh l'amour pop disco and also praised Say What and Love Is a Loser. A reviewer for Sounds was scathing. Later Who Needs Love Like That and Oh l'amour did reach high positions after all, in remixed form.
werk/erasure-wonderland.listen: Listen to Oh L'Amour and notice the pop-disco character of the song: the danceable rhythms and the glossy synthesizers.

werk/eric-clapton-no-reason-to-cry.text:
No Reason to Cry is Eric Clapton's fourth solo album and was released on 27 August 1976 on RSO Records. It was recorded between December 1975 and May 1976 in Malibu and Los Angeles, with sessions in March 1976 at The Band's Shangri-la Studios. All five members of that group took part. Rick Danko sings All Our Past Times together with the guitarist; they wrote it together.

Bob Dylan appears as a duet partner in Sign Language, with a song that has not been released elsewhere. According to the booklet of a Dylan box set, he simply wandered around and stayed in a tent in the garden. Marcy Levy sings Innocent Times and shares the vocals in Hungry. Critics responded moderately. AllMusic called it ordinary pop and rock, with the finest music where guests join in. The album reached number 8 in the United Kingdom and number 15 in the United States.
werk/eric-clapton-no-reason-to-cry.listen: Listen to Sign Language and notice the two voices: this is a duet with Bob Dylan, who wrote the song.

werk/eric-dolphy-caribe.text:
Caribé is an album by the Latin Jazz Quintet with Eric Dolphy, recorded in 1960 and released in February 1961 on the label New Jazz. The group around conga player Juan Amalbert also consists of pianist Gene Casey, vibraphonist Charlie Simons, bassist Bill Ellington and drummer Manny Ramos. Esmond Edwards supervised and Rudy Van Gelder recorded it. As a guest, he plays alto saxophone, flute and bass clarinet.

AllMusic compared the record to a stick of dynamite at a quiet dinner that nevertheless disturbs nothing: not an ideal combination, but certainly fascinating. The biographers Vladimir Simosko and Barry Tepperman thought the solos by Casey and Simons good, but the strongest voice on the session was that of the horn player. He really plays along with the group and does not give up his own approach.
werk/eric-dolphy-caribe.listen: Listen to Caribé, at just over ten minutes the longest track, and notice how the horn player relates to the congas and the rhythm of the group.

werk/eric-dolphy-far-cry.text:
Far Cry is Eric Dolphy's third album and was released in 1962 on New Jazz, a sister label of Prestige. He co-led the quintet with trumpeter Booker Little, and it is one of the few recordings of their collaboration. Pianist Jaki Byard, bassist Ron Carter and drummer Roy Haynes had already been heard on his albums before. It was a busy time: he played on Ornette Coleman's Free Jazz and recorded this album on the same day.

The whole first side is a tribute to Charlie Parker. Byard wrote Mrs. Parker of K.C. for Parker's mother and Ode to Charlie Parker. Miss Ann is a musical portrait of a girl Dolphy knew, and it is his best-known composition. In Tenderly he plays alone on alto saxophone, unaccompanied. According to Stuart Nicholson, his style grew out of bebop and Parker, and was not opposed to them, as many critics then thought. Little died ten months later.
werk/eric-dolphy-far-cry.listen: Listen to Tenderly, where Dolphy plays alone on alto saxophone. Can you hear how the melody remains recognisable while he treats it freely?

werk/eric-dolphy-out-there.text:
Out There was released in September 1961 on Prestige Records and was only Eric Dolphy's second album as a leader. He had shortly before played with Charles Mingus. On this album he is in a quartet with cellist Ron Carter, who had then only just begun to be heard on records, bassist George Duvivier and drummer Roy Haynes. There is no piano or guitar. As a result he and Carter solo only above bass and drums, and the music sounds freer than on Outward Bound, which did include pianist Jaki Byard.

Dolphy wrote four of the tracks himself. There are also pieces by Mingus, Randy Weston and Hale Smith. In Eclipse he solos, rarely enough, on clarinet. The DownBeat reviewer of the day heard an improvement in his bass clarinet. Later Michael G. Nastos of AllMusic wrote that the music had a depth and a purpose that remained unique.
werk/eric-dolphy-out-there.listen: Listen to Serene and notice the bass clarinet and the cello above bass and drums. What do your ears miss, or not miss, without a piano?

werk/eric-dolphy-out-to-lunch.text:
Out to Lunch! is the only record Eric Dolphy made as a leader for Blue Note, and it was released only after his death. He played in a quintet with trumpeter Freddie Hubbard, vibraphonist Bobby Hutcherson, bassist Richard Davis and the drummer Tony Williams, only eighteen years old. According to Dolphy, everyone on this session was a leader. Shortly afterwards he left for Europe, where he died in West Berlin on 29 June 1964.

Hat and Beard is a tribute to Thelonious Monk, with wild bass clarinet playing and a percussive interlude by Williams and Hutcherson. In Gazzelloni, named after his flute teacher, everyone sticks to the theme for the first thirteen bars, after which freedom follows. In the title piece the pulse is suggested rather than played. Straight Up and Down was meant to evoke a drunken stagger. Critics count the record among Blue Note's best and among the high points of 1960s avant-garde jazz.
werk/eric-dolphy-out-to-lunch.listen: Listen to Hat and Beard and notice how the bass clarinet fans out wildly, and then hear the percussive interlude from the drums and the vibraphone.

werk/eric-dolphy-outward-bound.text:
Outward Bound is Eric Dolphy's debut under his own name, from 1960. The quintet recorded it at Van Gelder Studio in New Jersey, with trumpeter Freddie Hubbard, pianist Jaki Byard, bassist George Tucker and drummer Roy Haynes. Hubbard had shared a home with him when they first arrived in New York. The cover is by his friend Richard Prophet Jennings. The music is bebop-oriented and less adventurous than much of his later work. Of the three original pieces, G.W. is dedicated to bandleader Gerald Wilson, Les is named after trombonist Lester Robertson and 245 is a house number in Brooklyn.

Critics responded enthusiastically. Martin Williams wrote that from the first track it was clear that a fresh and important talent had arrived. PopMatters called the record the best place to start with this musician.
werk/eric-dolphy-outward-bound.listen: Listen to G.W. and notice the lightning-fast alto saxophone solo that breaks free from the melody while the rest of the band plays an ordinary bop accompaniment.

werk/erykah-badu-baduizm.text:
Baduizm is Erykah Badu's debut, released in 1997. She left her studies at Grambling State University to focus on music, toured with her cousin and recorded a nineteen-track demo, Country Cousins. That led her to Kedar Massenburg, who arranged a duet with D'Angelo and signed her to Universal. Recording ran from January to October 1996, in New York, Philadelphia and Dallas. Just before the release she was dissatisfied and worked in Philadelphia with The Roots, which produced Otherside of the Game and Sometimes.

The album mixes soul and jazz with hip hop beats. Critics saw in it the simplicity of early-1970s soul and compared her singing with that of Billie Holiday. On & On, the first single, became a hit. The record won a Grammy for Best R&B Album and contributed to the visibility of neo soul.
werk/erykah-badu-baduizm.listen: Listen to On & On. Notice her loose, almost spoken singing over a calm groove, and hear how relaxed the song sounds.

werk/esbjorn-svensson-trio-good-morning-.text:
Good Morning Susie Soho is a studio album by the Swedish Esbjörn Svensson Trio, released in September 2000. Esbjörn Svensson plays keyboards, Dan Berglund bass and Magnus Öström drums, gopichard, percussion and tabla. The trio wrote all the tracks themselves, except The Face of Love, which is by Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, David Robbins and Tim Robbins. The album reached number 15 on the Swedish album chart.

The lengths vary widely: Serenity lasts under two minutes, The Wraith well over nine and Reminiscence of a Soul nearly twelve. The reception was glowing. Stuart Nicholson wrote in JazzTimes that the album was darkly lyrical and distinctly contemporary, and the magazine Jazzwise named it album of the year 2000.
werk/esbjorn-svensson-trio-good-morning-.listen: Listen to The Wraith, at over nine minutes one of the longest tracks, and follow how piano, bass and drums build the piece together.

werk/esbjorn-svensson-trio-winter-in-ven.text:
Winter in Venice was released in 1997 and is a studio album by the Swedish jazz trio Esbjörn Svensson Trio, also known by the abbreviation E.S.T. The line-up consists of piano, bass and drums, played by the bandleader, Dan Berglund and Magnus Öström. Johan Ekelund produced the record, which was released on the label ACT Music.

The album has thirteen tracks. A large part of them form the suite Semblance, which is spread across the record in four parts. There are also tracks such as Calling Home, Damned Back Blues and As the Crow Flies. In 1998 the album won the Swedish Grammy for best jazz album.
werk/esbjorn-svensson-trio-winter-in-ven.listen: Listen to the title track Winter In Venice and notice how piano, bass and drums work together as equal partners.

werk/esperanza-spalding-esperanza.text:
Esperanza is Esperanza Spalding's second studio album, released on 20 May 2008 by Heads Up International. She grew up among many cultures and sings on the record in three languages: English, Spanish and Portuguese. She plays acoustic bass, on two tracks a Doolin bass, and took care of the arrangements and the production. Guests included Donald Harrison, Ambrose Akinmusire and Gretchen Parlato, among others.

Critics praised the breadth of the record. Thom Jurek of AllMusic wrote that she broadens her musical adventure at every point, with taste, refinement and humour. Nate Chinen of Vibe found the album coherent and varied. After her Grammy for Best New Artist in February 2011 it entered at number 138 on the Billboard 200. It spent more than seventy weeks on the Top Jazz Albums chart.
werk/esperanza-spalding-esperanza.listen: Listen to Samba Em Preludio and notice Niño Josele's guitar alongside her voice and Doolin bass.

werk/esperanza-spalding-junjo.text:
Junjo is Esperanza Spalding's debut, released on 18 April 2006 on the Spanish label Ayva Music. She was 22 at the time and played double bass in a piano trio with pianist Aruán Ortiz and drummer Francisco Mela. She sings on all the tracks except two, often without words. Besides original compositions, the trio plays work by Jimmy Rowles, Egberto Gismonti and Chick Corea.

The music draws on jazz and on Brazilian and other Latin American styles. Michael Nastos of AllMusic called the record an exercise in joy and freedom. Jim Santella of All About Jazz praised her wordless singing and her conversational bass playing, and Jamie Katz of Vibe heard in her own compositions a new and important voice in jazz.
werk/esperanza-spalding-junjo.listen: Listen to Junjo and notice how her double bass and wordless singing interact with piano and drums, almost like a conversation.

werk/etta-james-at-last.text:
Etta James recorded her debut album for Argo Records, a label of the brothers Phil and Leonard Chess, who also produced the album. They believed that her voice could also appeal to the pop audience. For that reason many tracks were given an orchestral accompaniment, written and conducted by Riley Hampton.

The album combines blues numbers with jazz and pop standards. It includes Stormy Weather, A Sunday Kind of Love and Willie Dixon's I Just Want To Make Love To You. Four tracks were also released as singles: All I Could Do Was Cry, Trust In Me, At Last and My Dearest Darling. In At Last, according to one critic, the singer shifts from powerful blues shouting to light, airy phrasing. The album received glowing reviews, Rolling Stone called it an enchanting album, and many artists have since covered At Last.
werk/etta-james-at-last.listen: Listen in At Last to how the voice changes: at times powerful and raw, then soft and floating, while the orchestra keeps playing underneath.

werk/etta-james-queen-of-soul.text:
Queen of Soul is Etta James's fifth studio album. It was released at the end of 1964 on Argo Records and collected the singles she had released that year. It was her first studio album in two years, since Etta James Top Ten. Five arrangers worked on it: Riley Hampton, Bert Keyes, Cliff Parman, Al Pokonka and Phil Wright.

The record has ten tracks, five per side of the LP. The material comes from various writers, including Irma Thomas. Two tracks made the charts: Baby What You Want Me to Do and Loving You More Every Day. They entered the rhythm and blues chart and the Billboard Pop Chart. The music platform Allmusic gave the album four out of five stars.
werk/etta-james-queen-of-soul.listen: Listen to I Wish Someone Would Care and notice how Etta James makes a song by another writer her own.

werk/etta-james-the-second-time-around.text:
This is Etta James's second studio album, released in 1961 on Argo. Phil and Leonard Chess produced it, as they had her previous record At Last!. Riley Hampton was arranger and conductor of the orchestra. The LP had ten tracks, five per side.

As on At Last!, the producers put strings beneath her voice, which also won her a place on the pop circuit. Three singles were released: Don't Cry Baby, The Fool That I Am and Seven Day Fool. They became hits in the R&B and pop charts in 1961. The album also contains covers of pop and jazz standards, such as Dream. AllMusic gave the record four out of five stars.
werk/etta-james-the-second-time-around.listen: Listen in Dream to how the strings surround James's voice.

werk/europe-out-of-this-world.text:
Out of This World is Europe's fourth studio album and was released on 9 August 1988 on Epic Records. It followed the far more successful The Final Countdown. Ron Nevison produced the record, which was recorded in London, at Olympic Studios and Townhouse Studios. Guitarist Kee Marcello played for the first time, as successor to John Norum.

The first single, Superstitious, reached number one in Sweden and Norway and is regarded as one of the band's best-known songs. The album reached number 19 on the American Billboard 200. Reviews were mixed: one critic heard hard rock with all the rough edges worn smooth, another called it a series of impressive rockers. A tour of the United States ultimately never happened, because sales were disappointing.
werk/europe-out-of-this-world.listen: Listen to Superstitious and notice Kee Marcello's guitar solos.

werk/europe-the-final-countdown.text:
The Final Countdown is the third studio album by the Swedish rock band Europe and was released on 26 May 1986 on Epic Records. It is the first album with keyboard player Mic Michaeli and drummer Ian Haugland. Producer Kevin Elson worked with the band in Zürich, and later recording also took place in Stockholm, Atlanta and Berkeley. The title song goes back to an old keyboard riff by singer Joey Tempest, and the lyrics were inspired by David Bowie's Space Oddity. Michaeli layered two synthesizers on top of each other for that striking sound.

The band had meant the song as an opener for concerts. When the record company proposed it as the first single, it reached number one in twenty-five countries. Carrie, a power ballad that came out of a jam session, also did well. Reviews were mixed.
werk/europe-the-final-countdown.listen: Listen to The Final Countdown and notice how the keyboard riff opens the song and keeps coming back.

werk/europe-wings-of-tomorrow.text:
Wings of Tomorrow is the second studio album by the Swedish rock band Europe. It was released on 24 February 1984 on Hot Records in Sweden and on Epic Records in the United States. The album was produced by Leif Mases, who also worked as sound engineer.

The band consisted of singer and keyboard player Joey Tempest, guitarist John Norum, bassist John Levén and drummer Tony Reno. For Reno it was the last record with the group. The sound is hard rock with a solid guitar. One of the tracks, Scream of Anger, was originally called Black Journey Through My Soul. The cover is drawn by Peter Engberg, the photographs are by Magnus Elgquist and the design is by Camilla B.
werk/europe-wings-of-tomorrow.listen: Listen to Stormwind, the opening track, and notice how John Norum's guitar sets the tone before the vocals begin.

werk/eurythmics-be-yourself-tonight.text:
Be Yourself Tonight is Eurythmics' fourth studio album, released on 29 April 1985 by RCA. It was recorded largely in Paris, with sessions in Detroit and Los Angeles. The duo left behind the experimental, synthesizer-based sound of earlier records for a pop and rock sound with influences from R&B and Motown, with a more traditional band line-up. David A. Stewart produced and received awards for it. Annie Lennox traded her androgynous look for a blonde rock 'n' roll look.

Aretha Franklin, Stevie Wonder and Elvis Costello appear as guests. Four singles were released: Would I Lie to You?, There Must Be an Angel, Sisters Are Doin' It for Themselves and It's Alright. There Must Be an Angel became the duo's only British number one. No tour followed, because Lennox was recovering from nodules on her vocal cords.
werk/eurythmics-be-yourself-tonight.listen: Listen to Sisters Are Doin' It for Themselves and notice how the voices of Annie Lennox and Aretha Franklin complement each other.

werk/eurythmics-in-the-garden.text:
After the break-up of the Tourists, Annie Lennox and Dave Stewart started again in 1980, as Eurythmics. It began with a New Year's party in the studio of the German producer Conny Plank near Cologne. There they jammed with Robert Görl of Deutsch Amerikanische Freundschaft, while Jaki Liebezeit and Holger Czukay of Can listened in. Plank arranged a contract with RCA and produced the debut. Clem Burke of Blondie also played on it.

Stewart sold two guitars and bought a drum machine, a Space Echo and a synthesizer. Under the influence of Plank and his guests he recorded all kinds of sounds, such as playground sounds in English Summer and a typewriter in She's Invisible Now. The album was released in October 1981 and went unnoticed. Singles such as Never Gonna Cry Again and Belinda got stuck. Critics called the electronic atmosphere intelligent and accessible, but also heard that it was not yet the later Eurythmics.
werk/eurythmics-in-the-garden.listen: Listen in English Summer to the sounds in the background, such as the children's voices from the playground, and notice how they give the song an atmosphere of its own.

werk/eurythmics-revenge.text:
Revenge is Eurythmics' fifth studio album, released on 30 June 1986 by RCA in the United Kingdom. It builds on the sound of its predecessor Be Yourself Tonight and takes the duo even further towards a rock band style. Annie Lennox sings, David A. Stewart plays guitar and produced. Clem Burke plays drums and Michael Kamen wrote and conducted the orchestral arrangements.

The album yielded four singles. Missionary Man won the 1987 Grammy for Best Rock Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal, and Stewart was named British Producer of the Year at the Brit Awards. An extensive world tour followed, and a concert in Australia was later released on video as Eurythmics Live. The 2005 reissue contains Revenge 2, a very different version of the song Revenge from the debut album In the Garden.
werk/eurythmics-revenge.listen: Listen to Missionary Man and notice the harmonica and the solid band sound.

werk/eurythmics-sweet-dreams-are-made-of.text:
Annie Lennox and David A. Stewart built this album in a small studio in the attic of an old warehouse in London, where they lived and worked for seven months. After that they moved to a small room in Church Studios. Most of it went onto an 8-track recorder, with synthesizers, a sequencer and a drum machine. The whole record cost about 5,000 pounds. After a year and a half without success, it was their breakthrough, on both sides of the Atlantic.

The title track reached number two in England and number one on the American Hot 100. The video, popular on MTV, showed Lennox with gender-bending imagery. After that Love Is a Stranger, earlier a flop, was also re-released and became a hit. The Walk and This Is the House also became singles. Reviews were mixed to positive: some found the record strong and catchy, others felt something was missing. Stewart called the record one of the most important of 1983.
werk/eurythmics-sweet-dreams-are-made-of.listen: Listen to Love Is a Stranger and notice how the synthesizers and the vocals together carry the song.

werk/evan-parker-collective-calls-urban-.text:
Collective Calls (Urban) (Two Microphones) has as its subtitle an improvised urban psychodrama in eight parts. The saxophonist Evan Parker and the drummer Paul Lytton recorded it in April 1972 at the Standard Essence Co, a small loft space in London. Incus Records released the album later that year, and in 2002 it appeared on CD on Psi Records.

The saxophonist plays soprano and tenor saxophone and home-made instruments and uses a cassette recorder. Lytton adds percussion, electronics and sounds. One reviewer called the record full of astonishing sounds that remain enigmatic to this day. The duo seeks out the very quiet and the very loud, and the tracks form sharp contrasts. Each side of the original LP ends with a short piece with a sustained sound. According to the Penguin Guide to Jazz, they are absorbing, concentrated performances with a striking coherence.
werk/evan-parker-collective-calls-urban-.listen: Listen to Shaker for the tonal colours of the saxophone and the sounds of Lytton. Notice how long the sounds are sustained.

werk/evan-parker-from-saxophone-en-tromb.text:
This live album was recorded on 18 May 1980 at the Art Workers' Guild in London. Evan Parker plays soprano and tenor saxophone, George Lewis plays trombone. Incus Records released it later that year on vinyl. In 2002 a CD edition followed on the saxophonist's own label Psi, and in 2023 it was reissued on vinyl in remastered form on Otoroku, the label of Cafe Oto.

The album contains five improvisations, which have only a number as their title. One reviewer heard microtonal sounds and ethereal planes of sound, and praised Lewis for his exuberant virtuosity on the trombone and the saxophonist for his circular breathing. The Penguin Guide to Jazz Recordings gave four stars and called it one of the saxophonist's best recordings. The opening track received particularly high praise. Another reviewer spoke of two young masters, beautifully captured.
werk/evan-parker-from-saxophone-en-tromb.listen: Listen to From Saxophone & Trombone 1 for the interplay of saxophone and trombone. Notice the long, sustained sounds of the saxophonist.

werk/extince-spraakwater.text: In 1995 Extince, from Oosterhout in Brabant, had a top 10 hit with Spraakwater, with samples from De Fabeltjeskrant. It was the first Dutch-language hip hop record to become a big hit. Extince rapped playfully and proudly in Dutch, and showed that the language rhymes perfectly well. After the raw Amsterdam dialect of Osdorp Posse, a more cheerful side was now added. More and more young people began rapping in Dutch themselves.
werk/extince-spraakwater.listen: At the start, hear the voice of Meneer de Uil (Mr Owl) from De Fabeltjeskrant, and then how Extince plays with the sound of the Dutch words.

werk/falco-einzelhaft.text:
Einzelhaft is Falco's debut from 1982. In 1980 he, then still a member of Drahdiwaberl, signed a contract for three solo albums with producer Robert Ponger and manager Markus Spiegel. At the beginning of 1981 they began work on the record. They already had a melody for Der Kommissar. Reinhold Bilgeri was to sing it but refused, after which Falco took the song himself and wrote the lyrics within three days.

Der Kommissar was released in November 1981 and reached the top of the charts in more than twenty countries. It is regarded as an innovative and influential German-language rap song. Other tracks borrow heavily from David Bowie's Berlin trilogy: Nie mehr Schule uses the music of Speed of Life from Low, and Helden von heute is a rewrite of Heroes. Ganz Wien, the first single, reached number eleven in the Austrian Ö3-Hitparade.
werk/falco-einzelhaft.listen: Listen to Helden von heute and compare it with Heroes by David Bowie. What similarities do you hear?

werk/fatboy-slim-you-ve-come-a-long-way-.text:
In the 1990s Norman Cook bought obscure vinyl records and built a library of samples on floppy disks from the snippets he liked. With an Akai sampler and an Atari computer he edited them into collages. Usually he added the bass line himself and sampled the rest in big beat style. Together with his engineer Simon Thornton he finished the tracks in his studio in Brighton, the House of Love. This was his second album under the name Fatboy Slim.

It was released in October 1998 on Skint Records and became his worldwide breakthrough. Four singles reached the British top ten: The Rockafeller Skank, Gangster Trippin, Praise You and Right Here, Right Now. Critics praised the sound and style, the album topped the British chart and earned Cook a Brit Award in 1999. The title comes from an advertising slogan for cigarettes.
werk/fatboy-slim-you-ve-come-a-long-way-.listen: Listen to Praise You and notice how the different samples together form one song. Can you hear that the track is built from separate pieces?

werk/feist-the-reminder.text:
The Reminder is the third studio album by the Canadian singer-songwriter Feist. It was released on 23 April 2007 outside North America and on 1 May in the United States and Canada. In 2008 a deluxe edition followed with nine extra tracks, mostly remixes. One of the tracks, Sealion, is an adaptation of Nina Simone's 1964 See Line Woman. That song is about the life of a high-class prostitute.

The record yielded four singles: My Moon My Man, 1234, I Feel It All and Honey Honey. The big success came with 1234, which was heard in September 2007 in an Apple TV commercial for the iPod Nano. The song was written by Sally Seltmann. The video was filmed in one continuous take. Critics were enthusiastic: Rolling Stone put the album in its top 50 of 2007, it won the Shortlist Music Prize and two Juno Awards, and it was nominated for a Grammy.
werk/feist-the-reminder.listen: Listen to Sealion and bear in mind that this is an adaptation of a song by Nina Simone: what is new about this song?

werk/fela-kuti-zombie.text:
Fela Kuti released this Afrobeat album in 1976 in Nigeria on Coconut Records. A year later Creole Records followed in the United Kingdom. The record was a sharp attack on the Nigerian soldiers. With the image of the zombie he described how the army worked: following orders without thinking.

The people received the album with enthusiasm, the government was furious. A thousand soldiers attacked the Kalakuta Republic, the commune Kuti had founded. He was badly beaten, his mother Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti was thrown out of a window and died, and his studio, instruments and master tapes were lost. According to the source, this violence was probably a consequence of the record. Robert Christgau called the music true fusion. In 2025 Zombie became the first Nigerian album in the Grammy Hall of Fame.
werk/fela-kuti-zombie.listen: Listen to Zombie and follow the English lyrics. Who is meant by the zombies?

werk/fleet-foxes-fleet-foxes.text:
The band formed in 2006 in Seattle around the singer and writer Robin Pecknold and guitarist Skyler Skjelset. In 2007 they began recording, in the basement of Pecknold's parents and at keyboard player Casey Wescott's home. Producer Phil Ek guided the work, which took a year and was paid for by the group themselves. The band members recorded their parts between their day jobs and set up their guitar amplifiers in tepees. The album was already finished, but it was completely rewritten and re-recorded. In November 2007 it was done.

The sound blends folk, gospel, psychedelic pop and Sacred Harp, with an emphasis on group singing and unusual song structures. Pecknold described the mood as ignorant nostalgia, and drew inspiration from Bob Dylan and Brian Wilson. White Winter Hymnal is about friends who dropped him in high school. Critics praised the album lavishly and counted it among the best debut albums ever.
werk/fleet-foxes-fleet-foxes.listen: Listen to White Winter Hymnal and notice how the voices complement one another and how the singing takes over the work of strings.

werk/fleet-foxes-helplessness-blues.text:
Fleet Foxes hoped to release the second album as early as 2009, but tours caused delays and a rehearsal stint near Seattle cost the band 60,000 dollars without result. In the end the band recorded from April 2010, at various locations, with producer Phil Ek. Robin Pecknold wanted to sound less poppy and more groove-oriented, with the twelve-string guitar of Roy Harper's Stormcock as a model. It is the first album with bassist Christian Wargo and multi-instrumentalist Morgan Henderson, and the only one with drummer Josh Tillman, who later went solo as Father John Misty.

The music is indie folk, chamber pop and expansive folk rock. The influence of American roots gave way to psychedelic folk from 1960s Britain. The title song was released as a free download, and Battery Kinzie and Grown Ocean received attention before the release. Critics were very enthusiastic: The Guardian called the record almost ridiculously beautiful.
werk/fleet-foxes-helplessness-blues.listen: Listen to Helplessness Blues and notice how the folk-like sounds are built up spaciously and expansively.

werk/fleetwood-mac-future-games.text:
Future Games is Fleetwood Mac's fifth album and was released on 3 September 1971. The record was made in the summer of 1971 at Advision Studios in London. Christine McVie was now a full member. Jeremy Spencer had left abruptly in February 1971 to join the Children of God. After an audition the band chose the American guitarist Bob Welch, who plays here for the first time.

Without Spencer's Chicago blues and 1950s rock and roll, the music moved further away from the blues, towards the melodic pop sound with which the band would break through in America four years later. Four of the eight tracks are by Danny Kirwan, with Sands of Time as a complex example. Reprise did not want an album with seven songs, so What a Shame was hastily recorded as a jam. Welch's title song appears in the film Almost Famous.
werk/fleetwood-mac-future-games.listen: Listen to Future Games, the title track by newcomer Bob Welch, and notice how melodic and unbluesy it sounds.

werk/fleetwood-mac-kiln-house.text:
Kiln House is Fleetwood Mac's fourth studio album, released on 18 September 1970 on Reprise Records. It was the first record after the departure of founder Peter Green. The remaining members moved, with wives, children and road managers, to the English countryside, to a converted oast house for drying hops, which gave the record its name. In two weeks they recorded the album at De Lane Lea Studios. Christine McVie, then still Christine Perfect, took part, but was not allowed under contract to be credited as a musician.

Jeremy Spencer played a much bigger role than on the previous album. His humorous tribute to the 1950s, influenced by rockabilly and Sun Records, dominates the record. In addition, Danny Kirwan's songs are almost as prominent. Buddy's Song mentions titles by Buddy Holly, and Blood on the Floor parodies country and western.
werk/fleetwood-mac-kiln-house.listen: Listen to Buddy's Song and count how many Buddy Holly titles you recognise in the lyrics.

werk/fleetwood-mac-mr-wonderful.text:
The British blues group's second album was released in August 1968. It was much like the debut, but was recorded live in the studio, with amplifiers in front of microphones, a horn section and Christine Perfect of Chicken Shack on keyboards. Producer Mike Vernon put screens between the instruments to prevent spill. In total the recording took four days. Peter Green's tracks were recorded in one day, Stop Messin' Round in five takes. Jeremy Spencer sang six of his own songs and let the horns play freely. Four tracks open with the same Elmore James riff. The title came from a conversation in a restaurant about presenters who gush over their guests. Two earlier ideas, A Good Length and Udder Sucker, were rejected by the label.

After the great success of the debut, the reception was mixed. One reviewer called the blues sounds deep and exciting, but later the album was mostly called a disappointment.
werk/fleetwood-mac-mr-wonderful.listen: Listen to Dust My Broom and notice the guitar riff with which it opens. Can you hear how that Elmore James riff also begins other tracks on the record?

werk/fleetwood-mac-rumours.text:
After the great success of the 1975 album Fleetwood Mac, the band wanted to make a pop album that built on it. Recording began in February 1976 at the Record Plant in Sausalito, California, and ultimately lasted a year. It was produced by the band with Ken Caillat and Richard Dashut. In the meantime the band members had drifted apart: Christine and John McVie's marriage was over, and Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks had a quarrelling relationship. Hard drugs did not make the work any easier.

Those breakups colour the lyrics, which are about personal and often difficult relationships. The music mixes electric and acoustic instruments with striking rhythms. All four singles, Go Your Own Way, Dreams, Don't Stop and You Make Loving Fun, reached the American top ten. Critics praised the production and the harmonies of the three singers. In 1978 the album won a Grammy for Album of the Year.
werk/fleetwood-mac-rumours.listen: Listen in Go Your Own Way to how guitars and vocals together carry the song. Notice what the lyrics tell of a relationship falling apart.

werk/fleetwood-mac-then-play-on.text:
On this third album from 1969, Danny Kirwan plays for the first time, and it was the last with Peter Green. Jeremy Spencer hardly took part. Where the first two records were strict electric blues, the band now sought more variety: folk rock, hard rock, art rock and psychedelia. For the first time editing and overdubbing were used extensively. Green gave half of the writing to Kirwan. Underway, Searching for Madge and Fighting for Madge were assembled by Green from hours of studio jams. The title comes from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night. It was also the first release on Reprise Records.

The album reached number six on the British chart, the group's fourth consecutive album in the top twenty. Bonus tracks such as Oh Well were added later.
werk/fleetwood-mac-then-play-on.listen: Listen to Although the Sun Is Shining and notice Danny Kirwan's singing and guitar: how does his style sound different from the blues of the previous records?

werk/fleetwood-mac-tusk.text:
After the enormous success of Rumours, Lindsey Buckingham did not want a repeat. He resisted a sequel that Warner Bros. would gladly have had. Mick Fleetwood decided early on that it should be a double album. Buckingham was influenced by post-punk and bands such as Talking Heads. Some of his tracks, such as The Ledge, he recorded at home and played himself, and on some he used a tissue box as a snare.

The record sounded sparser and stranger than the previous album. Fleetwood Mac released it on 12 October 1979. The production costs were later estimated at 1.4 million dollars, at the time the most expensive rock album. The record company regarded sales of four million copies as a failure, compared with the ten million of Rumours. Later lists nevertheless include the record, and it is regarded as the band's experimental high point.
werk/fleetwood-mac-tusk.listen: Listen to The Ledge, recorded by Buckingham alone at home. What strikes you about how stripped-down it sounds?

werk/floating-points-promises.text:
Sam Shepherd, who makes music under the name Floating Points, heard Pharoah Sanders's debut record Elaenia in 2015. The saxophonist, then seventy-five, became friends with him, and together they conceived an album. Shepherd wrote the music and played many of the instruments himself. Recording took place in the summer of 2019 in Los Angeles. In the summer of 2020, during the pandemic, the London Symphony Orchestra recorded the strings in London.

The album is a single composition of more than 46 minutes in nine movements. It begins with a short sequence of notes on synthesizer, piano and harpsichord, which keeps returning. Sanders plays sparingly, atmospherically on tenor saxophone and sings wordlessly in the fourth movement. In the sixth movement the strings swell. Critics praised the dreamy atmosphere, and the album was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize. It was Sanders's last album.
werk/floating-points-promises.listen: Listen in Movement 4 to the voice of Pharoah Sanders, singing without words. Notice how it complements the saxophone and the repeating notes.

werk/flora-purim-butterfly-dreams.text:
Butterfly Dreams is the second studio album by the Brazilian jazz singer Flora Purim. It was released in 1973 on Milestone Records and recorded at Fantasy Studios in Berkeley, California. Orrin Keepnews produced. Purim was already part of the circle around Chick Corea at the time, and her vocal performances were eagerly awaited.

The accompaniment consists of musicians who suited her well: George Duke on electric piano and synthesizer, Stanley Clarke on bass, Joe Henderson on saxophone and flute and Airto Moreira on drums and percussion. Together they make light-sounding fusion with Latin American influences. According to AllMusic, Purim showed her voice here in all its qualities, and it was a high point in her career. Another reviewer praised the freshness of her voice.
werk/flora-purim-butterfly-dreams.listen: Listen to Butterfly Dreams and notice how Purim's voice floats among the instruments. Try to hear where she leads and where the band follows her.

werk/flora-purim-encounter.text:
Encounter is a studio album by the Brazilian jazz singer Flora Purim, released in 1977 on Milestone Records. It is a record with an exceptionally large guest list. Joe Henderson plays tenor saxophone, Raul de Souza trombone, McCoy Tyner acoustic piano and George Duke electric piano and synthesizer. Hermeto Pascoal plays electric piano and clavinet and sings along. Ron Carter plays acoustic bass and Airto Moreira drums and plays percussion on nearly all the tracks.

The line-up changes from track to track, so that jazz and electric sounds alternate. Scott Yanow of AllMusic gave the record four and a half stars and called it one of Purim's best jazz recordings.
werk/flora-purim-encounter.listen: Listen to Windows and notice how the singing relates to Joe Henderson's saxophone and George Duke's keyboards.

werk/flora-purim-stories-to-tell.text:
Stories to Tell is the fourth solo album by the Brazilian jazz singer Flora Purim. It was released in 1974 on Milestone Records. Her husband, percussionist Airto Moreira, led a large company of jazz and fusion musicians who assisted her.

Among them were George Duke on keyboards and synthesizer, Earl Klugh on guitar, bassist Ron Carter and, on one track, guitarist Carlos Santana. The album shows many sides of Purim: wordless singing that soars upwards, songs in English and Portuguese, brisk pieces full of percussion and quiet ballads. AllMusic gave the album four stars and noted the wide range of her abilities.
werk/flora-purim-stories-to-tell.listen: Listen to Insensatez and notice her voice and the language in which she sings. Hear how restrained the accompaniment remains in a ballad.

werk/flying-lotus-1983.text:
1983 is the debut album of the American electronic producer Steven Ellison, who works under the name Flying Lotus. The album was released on 3 October 2006 on Plug Research and is named after his birth year. Only Laura Darlington sings along, on the last track.

The music mixes influences from jazz harp, Japanese synth-pop, Afro-Cuban rhythms and distorted video game sounds. Critics praised the warm, expressive tone and the funk, although Pitchfork found the record mainly stylish and interchangeable with those of its contemporaries. Later a reviewer saw in 1983 a kind of calling card that set the tone for Ellison's later work. In 2026 an anniversary edition was released on vinyl.
werk/flying-lotus-1983.listen: Listen to Unexpected Delight, the track with Laura Darlington's vocals, and notice how her voice sits among the electronic sounds.

werk/flying-lotus-cosmogramma.text:
Cosmogramma is the third album by Steven Ellison, who makes music under the name Flying Lotus. He began recording in October 2008 in his apartment in Los Angeles, right after his previous album and the death of his mother. The title comes from a misunderstanding: his great-aunt Alice Coltrane spoke of earthly life as a cosmic drama, and he heard cosmogramma.

The album was released on 3 May 2010 on Warp Records. Ellison used a laptop, a sampler and a drum machine, but also live instruments such as harp, bass, strings and saxophone. Guests include Thom Yorke, Thundercat, Ravi Coltrane and Laura Darlington. The music is dense, layered and versatile. The critical response was very enthusiastic and the album appeared on many year-end lists.
werk/flying-lotus-cosmogramma.listen: Listen to ...And the World Laughs With You and notice Thom Yorke's voice amid the dense, layered production.

werk/flying-lotus-los-angeles.text:
Los Angeles is the second studio album by the American electronic producer Flying Lotus. It was released on 9 July 2008 on Warp Records and is named after his birthplace. The cover was designed by the British studio Build, with photography by Timothy Saccenti.

The press received the record very positively. On Metacritic the album scored an average of 81 from thirteen reviews, which indicates general acclaim. Resident Advisor put it third among the best albums of 2008, Fact tenth and Pitchfork 28th. In 2017 it was number 14 on Pitchfork's list of the fifty best IDM albums of all time.
werk/flying-lotus-los-angeles.listen: Listen to Brainfeeder, the opening track, and notice what kind of atmosphere it immediately sets for the rest of the record.

werk/flying-lotus-until-the-quiet-comes.text:
Until the Quiet Comes is Flying Lotus's fourth album and was released on 26 September 2012 on Warp Records. For two years he worked on the record at home in Los Angeles, mainly with Ableton Live. He drew inspiration from psychedelic music, African percussion and the subconscious and the dream world. He did not want to repeat himself: after the great energy of Cosmogramma he chose a more restrained, more intimate sound, with tension and release.

Guests are Erykah Badu, Thom Yorke and Laura Darlington, and bassist Thundercat is on board again. The tracks run into one another and are characterised by ghostly vocals, irregular drum patterns and vibrating bass lines. He got the idea of a journey by imagining that he was practising astral projection. Critics praised the complex music and his sound engineering.
werk/flying-lotus-until-the-quiet-comes.listen: Listen to See Thru to U and notice how Erykah Badu's voice relates to the irregular rhythms beneath it.

werk/flying-lotus-you-re-dead.text:
Steven Ellison, known as Flying Lotus, came up with the idea for this album with bassist Thundercat when they were listening to George Duke in the car and decided they should now make something like it themselves. He wanted to make the fastest, hardest and most intense jazz record and recorded it at his home in Los Angeles, with Ableton Live and real instruments. The album was released on 6 October 2014 on Warp Records. Thundercat plays bass on nearly every track, and guests include Kendrick Lamar, Snoop Dogg, Kamasi Washington and Herbie Hancock.

It is a concept album about death and the afterlife, mainly instrumental, with jazz fusion, electronica and hip hop. Ellison says the message is not that it is over, but that the spirits live on. Never Catch Me was released as a single. The critical response was very positive.
werk/flying-lotus-you-re-dead.listen: Listen to Never Catch Me and notice how Kendrick Lamar raps over a track with intricate, shifting rhythms.

werk/focus-hocus-pocus.text: In 1971 Hocus Pocus by Focus was released, the band of organist and flautist Thijs van Leer and guitarist Jan Akkerman. Both were technically strong musicians, but their best-known song turned out to be a joke: a hard guitar riff, a drum break, yodelling, whistling and a flute solo. In 1973 it became a hit in England and America. Prog rock with humour: English bands scarcely dared.
werk/focus-hocus-pocus.listen: Count the parts: riff, drum break, yodelling and flute solo. Just try playing it yourself.

werk/focus-mother-focus.text:
Mother Focus is Focus's fifth studio album, from 1975, on Polydor in Europe, Atco in North America and EMI in Japan. Some tracks depart from the prog rock of earlier records and point towards funk with a little light jazz and pop. The tracks are also shorter than before: the longest lasts 3:55. Bassist Bert Ruiter supplied most of the themes, because Thijs van Leer had just made a solo album, O My Love, and Jan Akkerman was holding back songs for his album Eli.

The closing track Father Bach is credited as traditional, but consists of the opening lines of Bach's Matthäus-Passion. Van Leer plays organ, piano, flutes and synthesizers, Akkerman guitar, Ruiter bass and David Kemper drums.
werk/focus-mother-focus.listen: Listen to the short closing track Father Bach and try to recognise the opening lines of Bach's Matthäus-Passion.

werk/foo-fighters-echoes-silence-patienc.text:
Echoes, Silence, Patience & Grace is Foo Fighters' sixth studio album and was released on 25 September 2007. After the tour for In Your Honor, with both acoustic and electric shows, Dave Grohl wanted a record that stepped out of the comfort zone. He brought back Gil Norton, the producer of The Colour and the Shape. Recording began in March 2007 at Studio 606 in the basement of Grohl's house. He finished writing The Pretender only during a break.

The album mixes hard rock with acoustic tracks and plays with dynamics: silences that burst into an explosion. The lyrics are about birth, death and life, inspired by the birth of Grohl's daughter. Ballad of the Beaconsfield Miners is the band's first instrumental track. The record won the Grammy for Best Rock Album.
werk/foo-fighters-echoes-silence-patienc.listen: Listen to Ballad of the Beaconsfield Miners. Notice that this is an instrumental track, in which the guitar takes the place of the vocals.

werk/foo-fighters-one-by-one.text:
The recording of One by One got off to a difficult start. After a hard time in which drummer Taylor Hawkins overdosed, the band recorded ten tracks in Virginia and later in Los Angeles, for more than a million dollars. Nobody was satisfied. The music sounded too clean and too tame, and quarrels broke out. In April 2002 the band threw everything away. After that Dave Grohl rescued the project in two weeks in his own studio, with Nick Raskulinecz as producer. Only Tired of You remained from the first sessions, with a guest appearance by Brian May.

The album was released on 22 October 2002 and sounds harder and more direct than the earlier records. Grohl wanted to capture the energy of the live shows. It was the first record with guitarist Chris Shiflett. The singles All My Life and Times Like These did well. The album won the Grammy for Best Rock Album in 2004.
werk/foo-fighters-one-by-one.listen: Listen to All My Life and notice how the verse begins quietly and the chorus sweeps over it with full force.

werk/foo-fighters-the-colour-and-the-sha.text:
On Foo Fighters' first album, Dave Grohl still played almost everything himself. For the follow-up he brought in guitarist Pat Smear, bassist Nate Mendel and drummer William Goldsmith, so that the album became the first record actually made as a band. Producer Gil Norton, known for his work with the Pixies, was to give it more pop gloss. The first sessions at Bear Creek Studio in Washington went badly, and almost everything was thrown away. In Hollywood the band re-recorded most of it in early 1997, now with Grohl himself behind the drums. Goldsmith left shortly afterwards.

The lyrics are mostly about Grohl's divorce in 1996. The running order of the tracks is meant as a therapy session, with fast songs and ballads side by side. Monkey Wrench, Everlong and My Hero became the singles. Critics saw it as an important American rock record of its time.
werk/foo-fighters-the-colour-and-the-sha.listen: Listen in Monkey Wrench to the hard guitars and the drums, which Grohl played himself. Notice how full and direct the band sounds.

werk/foo-fighters-there-is-nothing-left-.text:
After the difficult recording of The Colour and the Shape, Foo Fighters lost two band members. Dave Grohl fired guitarist Franz Stahl and turned the group into a trio with bassist Nate Mendel and drummer Taylor Hawkins. He bought a house in Alexandria, Virginia, and built Studio 606 in the basement, with no record company looking over his shoulder. Together with producer Adam Kasper the band recorded the album there, without computer programs such as Pro Tools. It was released on 2 November 1999.

The sound is softer and more melodic than before. Grohl called it his favourite album by the band. Learn to Fly became the first single. According to Allmusic, the group sounds for the first time like one tight band, which also rocks hard. In 2001 the album received the Grammy for Best Rock Album, the band's first Grammy.
werk/foo-fighters-there-is-nothing-left-.listen: Listen to Aurora and notice the drumming: Taylor Hawkins plays the more jazzy parts here, by his own account.

werk/foreigner-double-vision.text:
Double Vision is Foreigner's second album. It was recorded between March and May 1978 and released on 20 June 1978 on Atlantic Records. It is the only album co-produced by Keith Olsen and the last with bassist Ed Gagliardi, who was later replaced by Rick Wills. There is a joke attached to the title: A&R man John Kalodner had his name in the credits twice, at Mick Jones's suggestion.

The singles were Hot Blooded (number 3 on the American Hot 100), Double Vision (number 2) and Blue Morning, Blue Day (number 15). Tramontane is the only instrumental track the band has released on a studio album. Jones sings lead himself on Back Where You Belong and I Have Waited So Long. Critics saw the album as a continuation of the debut: one spoke of slick production without artistic depth, another of hard rock at its best.
werk/foreigner-double-vision.listen: Listen to Tramontane, the only instrumental track, and notice the heavy keyboard part and how the band members take turns in the spotlight.

werk/foreigner-foreigner.text:
The debut album of the British-American band Foreigner was released on 8 March 1977 on Atlantic. Guitarist Mick Jones had already written several songs before the band existed. Singer Lou Gramm sang three of them during his audition: Feels Like the First Time, Woman Oh Woman and At War with the World. Jones wanted Roy Thomas Baker as producer, but he had no time. Gary Lyons and John Sinclair of Sarm Studios therefore took on the production, together with Jones and Ian McDonald. The first mix in London was not liked, so the album was remixed at Atlantic Recording Studios.

Three tracks became hits: Feels Like the First Time, Cold as Ice and Long, Long Way from Home. In Starrider, Jones sings lead himself, something that rarely happens. Reviews varied. One reviewer found the production tight but the band's own vision too thin, while AllMusic later praised the craftsmanlike rock work.
werk/foreigner-foreigner.listen: Listen to Starrider and notice the singing: here guitarist Mick Jones sings the lead part himself instead of Lou Gramm.

werk/foreigner-head-games.text:
Head Games, released in September 1979 on Atlantic, is Foreigner's third studio album. It was recorded in New York and mixed in Los Angeles. It is the only album the band made with Roy Thomas Baker, known for the records of Queen. Bassist Rick Wills took the place of the dismissed Ed Gagliardi. It was also the last record with founders Ian McDonald and Al Greenwood and the last with vocals by guitarist Mick Jones, on The Modern Day.

The single Dirty White Boy preceded the album and reached number 12 on the American Hot 100. The album itself reached number 5 and went platinum within four months. The cover, with Lisanne Falk as the model, was criticised by feminists, while singer Lou Gramm said it was meant to be cute like a cartoon. Reviews were divided. Later Classic Rock called Rev on the Red Line an underrated track.
werk/foreigner-head-games.listen: Listen to Rev On the Red Line and notice Mick Jones's guitar solo, which one reviewer called sparkling.
